question: Arctic foxes in northern Canada have thick white fur that provides insulation and camouflage in snowy environments. As climate change causes earlier spring snowmelt and reduced snow cover duration, some fox populations are experiencing higher predation rates during spring months. Which of the following best explains this pattern?
answers: Earlier snowmelt exposes dark, snow-free ground before foxes have molted their white winter coats, making the foxes visually conspicuous to predators despite possessing camouflage that is normally adaptive
Earlier snowmelt causes foxes to lose their white fur prematurely and permanently, forcing an evolutionary shift to darker fur that reduces insulation during remaining snowy periods
Reduced snow cover allows predators to hunt more effectively year-round, and foxes can adapt by developing darker fur within a single generation to compensate
Earlier snowmelt increases the availability of plant food sources for foxes, which reduces local predator populations and therefore lowers predation pressure

question: A nocturnal predator suddenly appears in an insect population's habitat. Some insects carry a heritable allele for daytime (diurnal) activity while others remain nocturnal by default. How will the population most likely respond to this new predation pressure over multiple generations?
answers: The frequency of the day-active allele will likely increase over generations, because diurnal individuals are more likely to survive and reproduce by avoiding nocturnal predation
The population can become fully diurnal within a single generation, since genetic change occurs immediately in response to new predation pressure
Individuals may shift their activity timing through learned behavior, and such learned behavioral shifts are passed on genetically to their offspring
The nocturnal predator will inevitably starve within a few generations, since natural selection guarantees prey populations always outpace predator adaptation

stimulus.title: Insect Population Response to a New Nocturnal Predator

question: Prey species such as ground squirrels that exhibit vigilance behaviors—frequently scanning for predators—have higher survival rates than less vigilant individuals in the same population. Over multiple generations, vigilance behaviors become more common in the population. Which of the following best explains this pattern?
answers: Vigilant individuals detect predators earlier and survive at higher rates, but vigilance frequency remains constant in the population because vigilant individuals spend less time foraging and produce fewer offspring.

Vigilant individuals detect predators earlier and survive at higher rates, passing genes for vigilance to offspring and increasing the frequency of vigilant behavior in the population through natural selection.
Vigilant individuals have higher survival rates because they spend less energy on vigilance and more energy on reproduction, allowing them to produce more offspring.

Vigilance behaviors increase survival in environments with high predator density, but this behavioral adaptation only occurs within individual organisms during their lifetime and is not heritable across generations.

question: Researchers studying beak size evolution in Darwin's finches on the Galápagos Islands collected data on beak depth and body size for 200 individual finches across five species over a 20-year period. They measured beak depth using calipers and recorded measurements annually during the breeding season. Which of the following best describes the research method used in this study?
answers: Longitudinal observational study tracking individual beak development within the same finches over their lifespans
Longitudinal observational study tracking morphological traits across populations over time
Retrospective observational study tracking morphological traits by analyzing museum specimens collected over a 20-year period
Longitudinal experimental study manipulating environmental conditions to track morphological trait changes across populations over time

question: A study investigates how root depth affects survival in drought-adapted grasses. Researchers plant three grass species with different average root depths (10 cm, 30 cm, 50 cm) in identical soil plots and withhold water for 30 days. What is the dependent variable?
answers: The average root depth of the three grass species
The duration of water withholding during the study
The survival rate of the grass species after 30 days
The soil composition used in the identical plots

question: An ornithologist shows migratory birds have genetically programmed navigation and seasonal timing consistent across populations and generations. Which choice best describes the reasoning that migration is an adaptation to seasonal change?
answers: It wrongly attributes migration evolution to recent human caused climate change.
It mistakes innate genetic programming for learned behavior becoming inherited.
Inherited navigation and timing show migration evolved by natural selection.
It wrongly assumes genetic basis makes migration completely inflexible to environment.

question: To test if a mosquito population has evolved resistance to DDT, researchers expose 50 mosquitoes to a standard dose and record mortality. They repeat this procedure with 10 different groups of 50 mosquitoes from the same population. What is the primary purpose of using multiple groups?
answers: To increase the sample size and improve the statistical power of the experiment
To account for natural variability in mosquito survival rates
To determine whether resistance levels vary among different subpopulations within the same location
To control for environmental factors that might affect DDT effectiveness across trials

question: A disease ecologist reports plague outcomes in two prairie dog colonies with different genetic diversity: Colony A had 200 individuals and a genetic diversity index of 0.45; Colony B had 180 individuals and an index of 0.72. After plague spread through both colonies, Colony A suffered 95% mortality (10 survivors, all carrying a rare resistance allele), while Colony B suffered only 40% mortality. Which conclusion is best supported by this comparison?
answers: Populations with lower genetic diversity, like Colony A, may lack sufficient variation for disease resistance and can suffer catastrophic mortality when a novel pathogen appears, compared to more genetically diverse populations
Small population size alone, independent of genetic diversity, fully explains the difference in mortality observed between Colony A and Colony B
The survival of 10 individuals in Colony A demonstrates that the colony's overall population is not at meaningful risk of further decline
Genetic diversity has no measurable relationship to disease outcomes; the difference between colonies is best explained by chance alone

stimulus.title: Prairie Dog Colony Outcomes After Plague Exposure

question: A researcher studying behavioral adaptation to predation in beetles placed beetles from a high-predation forest population and a low-predation forest population into identical experimental chambers, introduced a predatory spider into each chamber, and recorded whether beetles fled, froze, or were captured. In this experiment, what is the independent variable?
answers: The population origin of the beetles (high-predation versus low-predation forest)
The body size of the beetles sampled from the two different forest populations
Whether individual beetles survived the encounter with the predatory spider
The species of predatory spider that was introduced into each experimental chamber

question: Estuarine fish face fluctuating salinity and evolve genetic variants for flexible osmoregulation. Which best explains how this trait is an adaptation to the estuary environment?
answers: Fish in stable marine habitats evolve flexible osmoregulation despite constant salinity.
Alleles for flexible osmoregulation increase survival and reproduction in variable salinity.
Thicker skin blocking water and salt exchange is not a known fish mechanism.
Flexible osmoregulation provides no advantage because fish cannot reproduce in fluctuating salinity
